title: Log stream retention and admin guardrails for RBAC v2 + SSO attributes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: With RBAC v2 and richer SSO/SAML attributes we must ensure audit logs capture admin-level intent while avoiding unbounded storage growth / PII exposure. Current audit pipeline writes verbose events into a shared hot index with no sensitivity-aware retention. That causes cost spikes and creates compliance risk when tenant admin actions (sensitive) are treated the same as low-value telemetry.

Goal: Build an ingestion+storage policy layer that uses RBAC v2 role and SSO group attributes to: 1) tag events with sensitivity and retention class, 2) route admin/sensitive streams into compacted, longer-retain indexes with stricter access controls and KMS-wrapped encryption, and 3) apply cost-aware cold-tiering for low-sensitivity telemetry. Provide admin guardrails so org admins can set retention overrides and view cost impact in Console.

Scope: ingestion tagging rules, partition/index naming, TTL/ILM policies, compactification pass for admin action events, admin overrides via Console, backpressure signals to pipeline on quota/role limits, and migration plan for existing indices.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion adds 'sensitivity' and 'rbac_role' fields derived from access token + SAML group mapping for >= 95% of events
Admin-level events (roles: org_admin, infra_admin) are routed to 'audit-admin-YYYY.MM' indices which have encryption-at-rest, restricted index ACLs, and 3-year default retention
Telemetry events are routed to 'audit-telemetry-YYYY.MM' with compact-ttl of 90 days and move-to-cold at 14 days
Console exposes an 'Audit Retention' panel where org admins can request a per-org override (up to limits) and see projected monthly storage delta
Pipeline responds to 'retention_quota_exceeded' signal by throttling non-sensitive ingestion and emitting an alert to infra on-call
Migration plan and zero-downtime reindex job documented and test-run on staging cluster with <5% ingest amplification during reindex
technical_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs:

- Tagging source: prefer token/claim-sidecar enrichment in edge proxy (fast path) rather than post-ingest enrichment to avoid reindexing. We will extend the auth proxy to attach 'redwood.saml_groups' and 'redwood.rbac_role' to events.

- Indexing: adopt time-based indices with semantics: audit-admin-YYYY.MM (sensitive, long retention), audit-sensitive-YYYY.MM (sensitivity but not admin), audit-telemetry-YYYY.MM (low sensitivity). Use ILM policies to control retention and segment merging.

- Partitioning vs per-tenant indices: choose shared indices with tenant and sensitivity shard keys to limit shard explosion. We will allocate tenant->shard mapping via a consistent hash that keeps hot tenants pinned. Trade-off: increased cross-tenant query complexity vs shard count control.

- Compaction: implement periodic 'compactify' job that rewrites admin events into a dense, tokenized log format (drop redundant fields, compressed JSONB) to reduce storage without losing essential auditability. This job will run in off-peak windows and produce a compact snapshot index.

- Security controls: admin indices will have KMS-wrapped keys, restricted role mappings (RBAC v2 policies require 'audit.read:admin' to query), and audit of audit-reads. Access to compact indices will be logged separately.

- Cost accounting: emit 'storage_class' and 'estimated_storage_bytes' at roll time; Console will sum by org and role to show cost attribution.

- PII handling: SSO group mappings can mark an event as 'contains_pii' based on identity attributes. For 'contains_pii' true, we will enforce stricter ttl and optional redaction pipelines (configurable per-org).

- Backpressure: extend the ingestion pipeline to honor 'ingest_budget' metadata per org derived from billing/commit. When budget is exceeded, non-sensitive telemetry will be dropped or sampled; admin events are always preserved (unless legal hold is not configured).

Implementation notes:
- Auth proxy change: PR drafted (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/1321).
- ILM policy templates in infra repo: infra/indices/ilm/audit_ilm_v2.yml.
- Compactify tool: proto in tools/compactify-admin-logs (golang), needs perf bench.

Open questions:
1) Should admin override allow >3yr retention for legal holds? Pro: compliance; Con: unbounded cost. Proposed: support limited legal-hold workflow via support ticket and manual approval.
2) How to handle historical events that lack SSO claims? Proposed: best-effort reindexing with heuristics (user-agent mapping) and flagging unknowns for manual review.
progress_updates: 2025-10-13: Kickoff meeting with Security, Infra, and Console. Agreed on tagging model and index naming conventions.
2025-10-21: Auth proxy prototype sends saml_groups claim for staging; integration tests added (PR #1321).
2025-10-29: ILM templates reviewed by infra; compactify design doc shared internally (confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUD/Compactify+Design).
2025-11-02: Benchmarked compactify on 1TB of admin logs; expected 4.2x storage reduction for admin event snapshots. Identified GC window tuning to avoid query regressions.
